answer: Florida Medicaid may conduct on-site reviews before approving your crossover provider ID, and as an enrolling provider you must permit unannounced on-site inspections of all your locations. The passages provided do not state what happens on the Medicare side if a review contractor spots fraud.

citations.quote: Acknowledgement that the Agency may conduct on-site reviews prior to approving the crossover provider ID number
Providers seeking enrollment or enrolled providers must permit the Agency to conduct unannounced on-site inspections of any and all provider locations.

gold_answer: Florida conducts site visits on all providers in the moderate or high screening risk categories before initial enrollment and at every renewal, and may visit any provider at its discretion. On the Medicare side, review contractors take corrective action for non-compliance, escalate for repeated or abusive patterns, and refer any evidence of fraud to the UPICs.
gold_quote: The Agency maintains the right to conduct site visits on any provider, at its discretion, in accordance with 42 CFR 455.432; however, site visits are conducted on all providers with "moderate" or "high" screening categories prior to initial enrollment and during every subsequent renewal. || Contractors shall analyze provider compliance with Medicare coverage and coding rules and take appropriate corrective action when providers are found to be non-compliant. For repeated infractions, or infractions showing potential fraud or pattern of abuse, more severe administrative action shall be initiated. At any time, evidence of fraud shall result in referral to the UPICs for development.

judge.rationale: The answer misses the key rule that site visits are mandatory for moderate- and high-risk providers before initial enrollment and at every renewal, and it fails to state the Medicare fraud referral to UPICs, but each claim it does make appears in the cited passages.

question: A new supplier is signing up with both Florida Medicaid and Medicare. Will Florida come inspect the office before approving, and what happens on the Medicare side if a review contractor spots fraud?
